latest_boss_checkpoint.research: R040 Mahdaviyeh et al., arXiv:2506.04377v1 / PMLR 330:15–42 (2026): full arXiv HTML reviewed; arXiv version license CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. The worst-case construction shows replay can move error onto other old samples (O(1/T) to Θ(1)); the average-case result shows random replay can increase expected forgetting for certain task-subspace relationships; MLP/MNIST results are non-monotonic and task/sample-dependent. The result is conditional, not a universal anti-replay rule. No code or figures imported. R041 Thede et al., arXiv:2609.40089v1: full 31-page PDF reviewed. RoD jointly top-k selects adaptation by current loss minus specialist reference and replay by current loss minus pretrained reference; references are precomputed/hash-keyed; each step scores m*k candidates with a forward-only pass (m=2 in the paper), then trains on k. Specialist reference has offline cost; a smaller source model can transfer a curriculum to a larger target. Limits: only replay-pool-covered forgetting is visible, LM loss is not downstream capability, proxy replay can misalign with task retention, and each experimental condition is single-seed (seed 42) despite cross-family/scale/domain replication. Main experiments use distributed NVIDIA B200 GPUs with count varying by model/setting. Public OSS repo exact main SHA 9ecc05173a4a5a8b872e18608c319df0eab5db81, Apache-2.0; NeMo-RL v0.6.0/Megatron/Ray/SLURM; no code/dependency imported and no Android evidence.
